# Talking-head edit: fillers and pauses out

A 30 s raw take cut to 20 s from an edit decision list: every “um”, false start and long pause is removed, and the captions are retimed onto the edited timeline. The strip at the bottom shows the raw take, what was cut and the playhead jumping over each cut. The speaker is a synthetic figure and the audio is a generated voice-like tone track that follows the transcript; there is no real speech.

- Type: Talking-head edit
- Skill: `magnifito-edit`
- Engine: `edit`
- Output: 1920x1080, 20.47 s, with audio
- Video: [`../videos/03-talking-head-edit.mp4`](../videos/03-talking-head-edit.mp4)
- Footage: synthetic, generated by the commands below. No camera footage is used.

## Recreate it with Claude Code

Install the plugin (see the repository README), open this folder, and give Claude this prompt:

> Here is a raw talking-head take of our presenter (work/raw.mp4) and its word-level transcript (transcript.json). Cut it into a tight 16:9 clip of about 20 seconds: remove the fillers (“um”, “uh”), the false start and every pause longer than 0.6 s, but never cut into a word and keep her meaning. Write the cuts as an edl.json, apply it, retime the captions onto the edited timeline and burn them in with the current word highlighted. Add a strip at the bottom that shows the raw take, each removed range with what was said there, and the playhead jumping over the cuts, so the client can see what we took out.

## Recreate it by hand

From the repository root, one command renders this example exactly as committed:

```sh
npm run showcase -- 03-talking-head-edit
```

Or run the steps yourself from `showcase/03-talking-head-edit/` (after `npm run build && npm link`):

```sh
node make-footage.mjs
mgvideo inspect work/raw.mp4
node apply-edl.mjs
mgvideo concat work/cuts/cut-01.mp4 work/cuts/cut-02.mp4 work/cuts/cut-03.mp4 work/cuts/cut-04.mp4 work/cuts/cut-05.mp4 work/cuts/cut-06.mp4 work/cuts/cut-07.mp4 -o work/edit.mp4
node overlay.mjs
ffmpeg -i work/edit.mp4 -framerate 30 -i work/overlay/%05d.png -filter_complex '[0:v][1:v]overlay=0:0:format=auto,format=yuv420p[v]' -map [v] -map 0:a -c:v libx264 -preset medium -crf 18 -c:a aac -b:a 160k work/final.mp4
```

The finished file is `work/final.mp4`. The config files in this folder are the inputs.
